clue.text: Idiot to listen to Observer bigwig (not really listening)

definitions.note: adjectival phrase describing someone who does not take things in

blocks.note: a clot is a stupid person
to hear something is to listen to it
the bigwig at a newspaper such as The Observer is its editor, ED

explanation.surface: Someone calls a senior figure at the Observer newspaper a fool for failing to pay attention.
explanation.walkthrough: The Observer is a British Sunday newspaper; ED is the usual short form of editor. The bracketed phrase at the end is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloth-eared is informal British slang for someone inattentive or hard of hearing, as if their ears were muffled.

clue.text: Bullies those with beef?

blocks.note: first meaning: intimidates, a verb
second meaning: cattle, the animals that carry beef on them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Beef' suggests a grievance, which fits bullies picking a fight; here it is literal meat on the hoof.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to intimidate them, and female cattle raised for meat carry beef.

clue.text: Road signs every so often involved God

indicators.note: taking something every so often means picking at regular intervals, so only every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A god seems to have had a hand in the placing of roadside signage.
explanation.definitionFit: Odin is the chief deity of Norse mythology, father of Thor and ruler of Asgard.

clue.text: Star perhaps loved by any he moved

indicators.note: moved suggests the preceding letters are shifted around into a fresh order

blocks.note: the fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: A celebrity adored by every man who encounters them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' reads as a celebrity in the surface; in the answer it is an astronomical object, which is why 'perhaps' is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is one example of an object in space such as a planet, moon or comet.

clue.text: German car tooted endlessly within earshot

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is dropped from the word for tooted

blocks.note: Audi is a German car manufacturer
blew a horn or whistle

explanation.surface: A German car sounded its horn close enough for someone to hear it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something audible can be heard, which is what being in earshot means.

clue.text: Timeless English aquatic bird on a lake

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
a tern is a seabird
taken as written
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: An English water bird is floating on a lake, an unchanging scene.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means the first pieces sit above A and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal means lasting forever, without beginning or end, so outside time.

clue.text: Extraordinary power sees prison term reduced, twice

indicators.note: the term, or end, being cut back means the last letter of the prison word is lost
twice tells us the shortened word is written down two times in a row

blocks.note: jug is slang for prison

explanation.surface: Some remarkable influence gets a jail sentence cut, and then cut again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prison term reduced' reads as a shorter sentence; really the term (end) of the prison word is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Juju is a West African word for a charm or fetish and the magical force attributed to it.

clue.text: Danube and Nile flowing? That’s beyond doubt

indicators.note: flowing suggests letters running freely out of their set order, as rivers do

blocks.note: the fodder, minus the joining word and

explanation.surface: Two great rivers are running, and nobody can dispute it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is part of the surface only; the fodder is the two river names.
explanation.definitionFit: Something undeniable cannot be disputed, so it is certain and beyond doubt.

clue.text: Nudist’s sea-swimming without support

indicators.note: swimming letters are moving about loosely, so they settle in a new order

blocks.note: the fodder, the possessive s included

explanation.surface: A naturist goes for a dip in the sea with no costume, nor anything to keep them afloat.
explanation.definitionFit: Unassisted means doing something alone, receiving no help or aid from anyone.

clue.text: ‘Substance’ and ‘limitless mass’, we’re told; time will tell

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it, so the words are judged by sound

blocks.note: weight in the sense of importance or substance
taken as written
a sea of people is a vast mass, and the ocean seems limitless

explanation.surface: Quoted phrases sound like a philosophy lecture before the speaker says only time will tell.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom advises patience: the outcome will become clear later, much as time reveals things.

clue.text: Notion discovered in review of encyclopaedia

indicators.note: discovered in says the letters lie uncovered inside the following word
a review looks back, so the hidden letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of the word

explanation.surface: A concept turns up in a critical write-up of a reference book.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a thought or concept, which is exactly what a notion is.

clue.text: What’s produced by conversion of us immoral lot?

definitions.text: What’s produced by conversion of us immoral lot?

indicators.note: converting something remakes it in a different form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, every letter used

explanation.surface: A preacher asks what will be saved when a crowd of sinners is converted to faith.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes what religious conversion of sinners is supposed to win; read as wordplay, conversion rearranges the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Religious conversion is said to save the eternal spirit within each person, which is what the clue's question points to.

clue.text: Frantic Met’s about to save people offering defences

indicators.note: something frantic is wild and disordered, so the letters next to it are jumbled
about means going around, so the jumbled letters wrap the next pieces

blocks.note: the possessive s included in the fodder
to bank money is to save it
men as people in general

explanation.surface: The Metropolitan Police, in a panic, mount a rescue of people protected by barriers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Met is London's Metropolitan Police, but here it just supplies four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Embankments are raised banks of earth that protect land against flooding, so they serve as barriers.

clue.text: Wench wanting to repeatedly lose weight to become delightful

indicators.note: losing more than once means the same letter goes from both of the first two words

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
W is the abbreviation for weight

explanation.surface: A young woman hopes to slim down and become more attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting' looks like desire in the surface; here it is taken literally as a word to be trimmed. 'to' before 'repeatedly' is surface glue.
explanation.definitionFit: Enchanting describes something charming that casts a spell of pleasure, which is delightful.

clue.text: Reckoning essence of native language is translated

indicators.note: the essence is the heart of something, so only the core of the phrase survives
translating turns words into a different form, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: two letters dropped from each end of the phrase

explanation.surface: Someone works out what the heart of a mother tongue is when it is rendered in another.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle here is the phrase stripped of its outer two letters on each side, leaving ten letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Reckoning, in the sense of assessing or calculating a value, is what evaluating means.

clue.text: One of two footballers, calm, returning with malice concealed

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word for calm is read in the opposite direction
something concealed is hidden inside, so the word for malice goes within the other

blocks.note: even as in an even temper
ill as in ill will

explanation.surface: A player comes back composed, hiding any spite toward opponents.
explanation.walkthrough: Gary and Phil Neville are brothers who both played for Manchester United and England.
explanation.definitionFit: Neville is the surname shared by the footballing brothers Gary and Phil, so it names either one.

clue.text: Bathroom features: abrasive hard sponges, primarily?

definitions.text: Bathroom features: abrasive hard sponges, primarily?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letter of each word is taken

blocks.note: loo is British slang for a toilet
the initial letters of four words

explanation.surface: A bathroom inventory lists rough, stiff scrubbing sponges as its main fixtures.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes what is found by a bath; 'Bathroom' yields the slang word for the toilet, and 'primarily' then takes initials of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Loofahs are rough dried plant sponges used for scrubbing skin, kept by the bath.

clue.text: Some narwhal I butchered to get seafood

indicators.note: some means only part, so a run of letters is lifted from the words that follow

blocks.note: spans the end of the whale's name, the pronoun and the start of the verb

explanation.surface: A hunter confesses to carving up a whale to put fish on the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Halibut is a large flatfish caught and eaten, so it counts as seafood.

clue.text: Stimulants: great amounts vessel contained

indicators.note: contained means held inside, so the word for vessel sits within the other word

blocks.note: tons of something is a great deal
an urn is a vessel or vase

explanation.surface: A shipping manifest lists large quantities of stimulants carried in a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Turn-ons are things that excite or arouse someone, acting on them as stimulants do.

clue.text: Wood that sang, perhaps (of birth, that is)

blocks.note: natal means relating to birth
i.e., Latin id est

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about a singing forest, with a bracketed aside about birth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wood' is the Hollywood actress Natalie Wood, who appeared in musicals such as West Side Story; 'perhaps' admits her singing voice was often dubbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Natalie is the first name of the film star Wood, who played singing roles on screen.

clue.text: Nary a little laugh for a loser

blocks.note: nary means not any
a single ho of laughter
as in so much per head, for each

explanation.surface: Someone who has failed gets not even a snigger of sympathy.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-hoper is someone with no chance of success, a person bound to fail.

clue.text: Hansel and Gretel running with wobbly legs away from brute

indicators.note: going away from means being taken out of, so the letters of legs leave the names
running suggests letters on the move, shifting out of their written order

blocks.note: the fairy-tale siblings, every letter
wobbly says these letters may be in any order where they appear in the names

explanation.surface: The fairy-tale children flee on shaky legs from a monster.
explanation.walkthrough: S, G, one E and one L come out of the names, scattered rather than together, which is why legs is wobbly.
explanation.definitionFit: Neanderthal is used informally for an uncouth or brutish person, after the early human species.

clue.text: Unpleasant odour of ancient pottery

blocks.note: first meaning: British slang for a bad smell
second meaning: porcelain from the Chinese dynasty of 1368 to 1644

explanation.surface: An old pot gives off a nasty whiff.
explanation.walkthrough: The smell sense is Scottish and northern English slang, as in minging for disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a bad smell in British slang and the porcelain of a Chinese imperial dynasty.

clue.text: Poet to look like a wolf, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: a wolf here is a predatory man who ogles

explanation.surface: A poet is told to ogle like a lecherous man.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Lear was the Victorian poet famous for nonsense verse such as The Owl and the Pussy-cat.

clue.text: Flower taken from Fair Isle

indicators.note: taken from says the letters are lifted straight out of the words that follow

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A bloom has been picked on a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: Fair Isle is a small island between Orkney and Shetland, known for patterned knitwear.
explanation.definitionFit: The iris is a garden plant with showy blooms, so it is a type of flower.

clue.text: Company minutes with potential to settle

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
M is the abbreviation for minutes
showing promise means having potential

explanation.surface: A firm's meeting notes show some prospect of reaching agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' sits inside the fragment because to show promise is to be with potential.
explanation.definitionFit: To compromise is to settle a dispute by each side conceding something to reach agreement.

clue.text: Primarily, geriatric and getting asinine?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letter of each word is taken

blocks.note: the initial letters of four words

explanation.surface: An elderly person is above all getting foolish in old age.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes an old person growing foolish; the initials spell the informal word for that.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaga is informal for senile or witless, especially an elderly person losing their faculties.

clue.text: One who looks at signs: 'logo-starer', fancifully

indicators.note: fancifully means in an imaginative, free way, so the letters are rearranged at will

blocks.note: the fodder, hyphen ignored

explanation.surface: Someone who studies the zodiac is mocked as a person who gazes at emblems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Signs' reads like logos or road signs; here it means the signs of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: An astrologer studies the zodiac signs and planetary positions to predict events.
